chunks: Ibn Mahboub, from Al-A'ala ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him)
Regarding the slave who gives wealth to a man to buy him so that he would emancipate him, he (peace be upon him) said: 'That is not correct for him'.
ai.seo_question: What is the validity of a slave giving money to a third party to buy their freedom?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) clarifies the mechanics of *itq bil-mal* (emancipation by payment), ruling that a slave cannot simply give money to a third party to purchase their freedom on their behalf. This highlights the Shia juristic emphasis on the direct contractual relationship between the slave and the owner, ensuring the transaction is clear and binding without intermediary ambiguity. The ruling underscores the importance of precise agency (*wakalah*) in manumission contracts within Islamic commercial law.

en.hubeali:
Ibn Mahboub, from Al A’ala Bin Razeyn, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far
<sup>asws</sup> regarding the slave who gives wealth to the man in order to buy him, so he would emancipate him. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘That is not correct for him’.
